text: Saul fully approved of putting him to death. That same day a great wave of persecution broke out against the Jerusalem church, and all except the apostles were scattered through the regions of Judea and Samaria.
Devout men buried Stephen and mourned deeply for him.
But Saul went about wrecking the church, entering house after house, dragging off both men and women and throwing them into prison.
Those who had been scattered went from place to place proclaiming the word.
Philip went down to a city in Samaria and began telling them about the Christ.
The crowds paid close attention to what Philip said, listening together and watching the signs he performed.
For unclean spirits came shrieking out of many who were possessed, and many paralyzed and lame people were healed.
So there was great joy in that city.
Now a man named Simon had already been practicing sorcery in that city, astonishing the Samaritan people and claiming to be someone great.
Everyone, from the least to the greatest, followed him closely, saying, This man is the power of God called Great.
They followed him because he had amazed them with his magic for a long time.
But once they believed Philip as he preached good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized.
Even Simon himself believed, and after his baptism he stayed close to Philip, astounded as he watched the great signs and miracles taking place.
When the apostles in Jerusalem heard Samaria had welcomed God's word, they sent Peter and John to them.
When they arrived, they prayed for the new believers to receive the Holy Spirit,
because the Spirit had not yet come upon any of them; they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, he brought them money,
saying, Give me this power too, so that anyone I lay hands on will receive the Holy Spirit.
But Peter told him, May your money be destroyed with you, since you thought you could buy God's gift with silver!
You have no part or share in this, because your heart is not right before God.
Turn from this wickedness of yours and pray to the Lord — perhaps he will forgive what you've been thinking.
For I can see that you are full of bitter envy and bound up in wrongdoing.
Simon answered, Pray to the Lord for me yourselves, so that none of what you've said happens to me.
After they had testified and proclaimed the Lord's word, Peter and John started back to Jerusalem, preaching the good news in many Samaritan villages along the way.
Meanwhile an angel of the Lord told Philip, Get up and head south, on the road going down from Jerusalem to Gaza — it runs through the desert.
So he got up and went. Along the way was an Ethiopian man, a eunuch of great authority under the Kandake, queen of the Ethiopians, in charge of all her treasury. He had come to Jerusalem to worship
and was now heading home, sitting in his chariot reading aloud from the prophet Isaiah.
The Spirit told Philip, Go up and stay close to that chariot.
Philip ran up and heard him reading from Isaiah, and asked, Do you understand what you're reading?
How could I, he replied, unless someone explains it to me? And he invited Philip to climb up and sit beside him.
The passage he was reading was this: Like a sheep he was led to be slaughtered, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, he did not open his mouth.
In his humiliation he was denied justice. Who can even describe his generation? For his life was taken from the earth.
The eunuch asked Philip, Tell me, who is the prophet talking about — himself, or someone else?
Then Philip began speaking, and starting from that very passage told him the good news about Jesus.
As they traveled along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, Look, water — what keeps me from being baptized?
Philip told him, If you believe with your whole heart, it's permitted. I believe, he answered, that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
He ordered the chariot to stop, and both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away, and the eunuch never saw him again, but continued on his way rejoicing.
Philip, however, turned up at Azotus, and as he traveled through the region he kept preaching the good news in every town until he reached Caesarea.
